body:
We should definitely special case this as we can not just drop the support.

> Am 03.11.2017 um 00:32 schrieb Scott Mitchell <notifications@github.com>:
> 
> 7995afe modifies HttpClientCoded#isContentAlwaysEmpty to return true if the statusCode == 101 which breaks the WebSocket V00 handshake [1]. The V00 handshake includes a payload in the request which is echoed back in the response. It could be argued that V00 is now irrelevant and folks should use the finalized RFC variant [2], but either way this feature is now broken. We have a few options:
> 
> Remove support for V00
> Special case this somehow when V00 is used
> Revert this fix
> Update the HttpClientCoded#isContentAlwaysEmpty to check against HttpStatusClass#INFORMATIONAL.
> Based upon the HTTP/1.x RFC [3] we shouldn't do 3, and we should actually also do 4.
> 
> Option 1 and 2 are debatable. It would be nice to do 2 because the V00 handshake is prohibited by the HTTP/1.x RFC.
> 
> [1] https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-ietf-hybi-thewebsocketprotocol-00
> [2] https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6455#section-1.3
> [3] https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-6.2
> 
> 1xx responses are terminated by the first empty line after
> the status-line (the empty line signaling the end of the header
> section).
> 
> /cc @pkolaczk
>

issue.body:
Motivation:

7995afee8f1cb9047709239321d84ccb279fe4d1 introduced a change that broke special handling of WebSockets 00.

Modifications:

Correctly delegate to super method which has special handling for WebSockets 00.

Result:

Fixes [#7362].
